commits.subject: phase 2 C48: drop Proposal.Valid, which every caller set to true
phase 2 C53: ActionDecided keeps only its Commit
phase 2 C54: signing holds the ML-DSA-65 key and signature lengths and the key check
phase 2 C68: a refused parameter certificate names its own causes

report.summary:
Run 'last' fixed C48, C53, C54 and C68 on branch p2-last, one commit per note, in worktree <scratch>/wt/p2-last. All four notes still applied to today's code, so no part was skipped.

C48 (38f03c8): consensus.Proposal no longer has a Valid field. The three checks are gone: the decide guard, the prevote-quorum guard and prevoteFor's `if proposal.Valid`. The comments on Proposal, ReceiveProposal and prevoteFor now say the caller passes only proposals whose block applied. The only node/ edits are the two `Valid: true` literals (startHeight and onProposal). The consensus tests got the same mechanical edit. I checked every path that hands the driver a proposal:
- onProposal runs ledger.ApplyBlock before ReceiveProposal.
- startHeight's held proposals come only from node.heightProposals, and only rememberProposal fills it, from three places: onProposal after ApplyBlock; the node's own proposals in process, which it signs only for a block in node.blocks (its ProposeBlock candidate, or a block that applied); and its own logged proposals. loadSignLog takes the logged ones only for the same height, so their block was built on the same pre-block state.
- The driver's own startRound proposes proposeValue (the ProposeBlock candidate) or validValue, a block it held a proposal of, or one it precommitted before a restart.

Every literal was already `Valid: true`, so behaviour is unchanged. Two lines in docs/reading-the-code.md that named Valid were updated (the Proposal row and the "decides only with a proposal its caller marked valid" bullet).

C53 (ac2578e): ActionDecided now holds only Commit. Node.commit reads decision.Commit.BlockHash and decision.Commit.Round (three lines in node/node.go), and so do driver_test.go and sim_test.go. The values cannot differ: VoteSet.Commit takes the set's height and round, and the hash with the strict ⅔ quorum, which is the proposal's hash the decide rule checked.

C54 (91ebb5c): signing/mldsa65.go exports PublicKeyBase64Length (2604), SignatureBase64Length (4412) and ValidPublicKeyBase64(key string) bool. That function decodes the key, checks for exactly 1952 bytes, and checks CanonicalBase64. Checking the length alone would not be enough: 2604 canonical characters also spell 1951 or 1953 bytes. The users of the new names:
- ledger/genesis.go uses ValidPublicKeyBase64. It drops crypto/mldsa and encoding/base64, so ledger no longer imports crypto/mldsa.
- ledger/name_request.go drops its own publicKeyLength and signatureLength; it and reassignment.go use signing's constants.
- cmd/server/config.go merges its publicKey size and spelling checks into one ValidPublicKeyBase64 check and drops crypto/mldsa (see deviations).
- ui/wallet.go's typedKey uses ValidPublicKeyBase64, and the update measure uses SignatureBase64Length. The wallet drops crypto/mldsa.

Outside signing, no Go file (review/ aside) now imports crypto/mldsa. One comment in ui/keyfile.go still names it; that file is outside this run's list. Two rows of docs/reading-the-code.md were updated: step 1 names the new exports, and step 8's shape row points to signing's constants.

C68 (afaa9de): incomplete(power, quorum, cause) takes its second sentence from the caller. With enough power, SubmitParameters now says "the parameters or the governance sequence these votes amend have moved since they were signed, or the new values are out of bounds for the current validators". SubmitReassignment keeps its old text, held in one local const for its two calls. docs/reading-the-code.md step 21's count went from 41 to 42, because the new test matches its ParameterVotes prefix. I checked every count in the guide against go test -list, and all match.

tests.name: signing: TestValidPublicKeyBase64TakesOnlyAKeyInItsOneSpelling (C54)
tests.failsWithoutChange: Yes. Without the change it does not compile, since ValidPublicKeyBase64 and the two constants do not exist. Scratch copies in p2-scratch/last-c54 show that each part of the check is needed. With a check of the length and the canonical spelling only, the test fails on the 1951-byte and the 1953-byte keys, both 2604 characters. With a check of the decoded size only, it fails on the key spelled with an embedded newline.

tests.name: ui: TestParameterVotesForAMovedSequenceNameTheirCause (C68)
tests.failsWithoutChange: Yes. Run against the parent commit 91ebb5c (p2-scratch/last-c68), it fails with: "the state these votes bind to has changed since they were signed, or the new key's proof is missing or does not verify".

tests.name: C48 and C53: existing consensus and node tests
tests.failsWithoutChange: Not applicable. Both notes are pure removals, so the guard is the existing tests passing after only the mechanical literal edits. TestDriver* and TestSim* now check decision.Commit.BlockHash against the proposed hash.

tests.name: C54 callers: existing genesis, config and wallet tests
tests.failsWithoutChange: Not applicable: the check moved into signing and refuses exactly the same keys. The genesis alias and non-base64 tests, the config alias test and the truncated-key test still pass. The truncated-key test's expected messages were rewritten for the new texts: "publicKey: not an ML-DSA-65 key in canonical base64" and "privateKey: ".

report.deviations:
1. C54, cmd/server/config.go: I removed the private-key (seed) length check instead of keeping it on crypto/mldsa.PrivateKeySize. signing exports no seed size, and the task says signing stays the one package that knows the scheme's sizes. The check only chose the error message, as its comment said since C29. NewSigner still refuses a wrong-length seed, now with "privateKey: mldsa: invalid seed length". That refusal comes later in load, after the genesis file is read, instead of before. TestLoadRejectsTruncatedKeys now expects "privateKey: " for the seed. The other reading is to keep crypto/mldsa in config.go just for that check, or to have signing export a seed length.

2. C54, error texts: the config message for publicKey is now "publicKey: not an ML-DSA-65 key in canonical base64, as keygen writes it (2604 characters)". Before, it was two messages, one giving the decoded byte count and one for the spelling. The genesis message now gives the 2604 characters instead of 1952 bytes. In both cases the keys refused are the same.

3. C54, ledger/name_request.go and reassignment.go: these keep their length-only shape checks, now on the signing constants. I did not switch them to ValidPublicKeyBase64. A wrong-size or non-canonical new key of the right length is still refused later, when its proof is verified (VerifyBase64 and MLDSA65.Verify). This is the smallest change and keeps the order of the checks.

4. C68: SubmitReassignment's first incomplete call, under !tally.Reached(), passes the same cause as its second call, held in one local const. At that call the power is always below the quorum, so the cause is never shown.

No edit was forced outside this run's file list.

report.openIssues:
- The owner should confirm the C54 reading for the server config: the seed-length check is removed and NewSigner's message ("privateKey: mldsa: invalid seed length") takes its place, as opposed to keeping crypto/mldsa in config.go for that one check.
- These sizes are still written outside signing, in comments, messages or test literals, all outside this run's list: the 32-byte seed in ui/keyfile.go's message and comment, 2604 in cmd/keygen's comment, and the 1952, 2604 and 44 in a few test literals in cmd/server/config_test.go and ledger/genesis_test.go.
- Run node2 is rewriting node/ at the same time. The merge needs three things from this run in node/node.go: the two Proposal literals without `Valid: true` in startHeight and onProposal (C48), and Node.commit reading decision.Commit.BlockHash and decision.Commit.Round (C53). If node2 moves or rewrites those lines, it must carry these edits.
- The guide's map of line counts (left to the orchestrator) is now off for consensus/driver.go, signing/mldsa65.go, ledger/name_request.go, cmd/server/config.go, ui/wallet.go and ui/admin.go.

problems.problem: C54 removed load's early check on the seed length. That partly reverses the owner's C29 decision, which kept the early key checks because their messages are clearer. A wrong-length seed now gets crypto/mldsa's bare message, and only after the genesis file has been read and validated. TestLoadRejectsTruncatedKeys now expects only the prefix "privateKey: ", which no longer says why the seed was refused. The builder justified this (signing stays the one package that knows the sizes) and flagged it as an open issue, so this is for the owner to confirm, not a defect.
problems.evidence: I ran a scratch test in <scratch>/p2-scratch/verify-last-2 that loads a config with a 16-byte seed and with a 64-byte seed. Both gave "privateKey: mldsa: invalid seed length". Before C54 the message was "privateKey: 16 bytes after base64 decode, want 32 (an ML-DSA-65 seed from keygen)". The note on C29 in review/phase2_code_notes.md says: "The early key checks stay, for their clearer messages." Nothing is accepted that was refused before: a wrong-length seed is still refused, and so is a mismatched pair.
problems.fix: Either the owner accepts the removal, or keep it size-free: wrap NewSigner's error in load with a hint, for example fmt.Errorf("privateKey: %w (the 32-byte seed keygen prints)", err) or a wording without the number, and have the test expect "seed" instead of the bare "privateKey: ".

verdict.evidence:
I verified branch p2-last at afaa9de (clean worktree) against review/phase2_code_notes.md C48, C53, C54 and C68, spec §0.2, §4.11, §8.2 and §9.1, and the C29 owner note.

What I ran and saw:
- On a scratch copy of HEAD (p2-scratch/verify-last-1), gofmt -l . printed nothing outside review/. go vet ./..., go vet -C ui ./..., go build ./... and go build -C ui -o /dev/null . all passed.
- On the same copy, GOLEDGER_CHAOS_SLACK=4 go test -race -count=1 ./... passed twice (consensus 56s and 58s, node 71s and 72s, ledger 15s). The same with -C ui passed twice (39s each). The -count=3 'Chaos|Restart|SignLog|Resume|CatchUp' run on ./node/ passed (90s). The log is <scratch>/p2-scratch/verify-last-suite.log.
- I exported each intermediate commit (38f03c8, ac2578e, 91ebb5c) to its own scratch copy. Each passed build, vet and gofmt, and go test ./... in both modules.

C48 (consensus safety). I traced every path that builds a Proposal for the driver; each already refuses a block that does not apply:
- onProposal runs ApplyBlock before rememberProposal and ReceiveProposal.
- node.heightProposals is written only by rememberProposal, which has three callers: onProposal after ApplyBlock; process, which proposes only blocks in node.blocks; and startHeight's logged own proposals. loadSignLog takes those only for the same height, checks each one's signature under the node's key and its block hash, and the pre-block state is the same.
- node.blocks is written only by the ProposeBlock candidate, by those logged proposals, and by onProposal after ApplyBlock.
- The sign log's Locked proposal goes back through onProposal.
- The driver's own startRound proposes proposeValue (the ProposeBlock candidate) or validValue. validValue comes from a held proposal, or from its own precommit before a restart.
- fastForward resets heightProposals.
Every literal was already Valid: true, so behaviour is unchanged. No `Valid: true` literal or `Proposal.Valid` read is left outside review/.

C53. ActionDecided has no other readers. VoteSet.Commit takes height and round from the set the driver built, and the hash from TwoThirdsMajority. Quorum is (2*total)/3+1, a strict two-thirds majority, so only one hash can reach it, and it is the proposal hash HasQuorumFor checked. Node.commit reads the same values as before.

C54. Outside signing, no Go file imports crypto/mldsa. I mutated ValidPublicKeyBase64 in a scratch copy:
- Dropping CanonicalBase64 makes TestValidPublicKeyBase64TakesOnlyAKeyInItsOneSpelling fail (the newline spelling passes), and the genesis tests TestGenesisRefusesDuplicateKeys and the a_key_in_another_spelling case fail too.
- Checking only the 2604-character length and the spelling fails on the 1953-byte key.
- With the right constants, the test checks the lengths of a real key and a real signature.
The callers refuse the same keys as before. A 2604-character string of 'A' is refused (it decodes to 1953 bytes), and so is an alias of the node's key.

C68. I added the new test to a copy of the parent commit 91ebb5c. It fails there with the old reassignment message ("...or the new key's proof is missing or does not verify"). The new message covers each way ParameterChange.Valid can fail once the power suffices: the digest, the sequence, Acceptable.

The guide's test counts. I checked every count go test -list can check against the root module and ui: 18, 17, 16, 13, 125 and 20 for consensus and ledger, and 17, 42 and 12 for ui. All match. Step 21's new count of 42 includes the new test. The node counts were not touched by this run and not checked.

The edited doc lines are accurate. In node/, only the two literals and Node.commit's three reads changed, and every file edited is within the run's list.

It fails with: error "privateKey: mldsa: invalid seed length" does not mention "privateKey: not an ML-DSA-65 seed, as keygen writes it". docs/reading-the-code.md step on cmd/server ('a key of the wrong size or spelling') is still accurate and was not changed.
notFixed: Part of the same minor problem, left for the owner: a wrong-length seed is still refused only after the genesis file has been read and checked, not before as it was before C54. To check it earlier, load would need the scheme before the genesis gives it, either by hard-coding signing.MLDSA65{}.ParsePrivateKey in cmd/server or by having signing export a seed size. C54's aim was that only signing knows the sizes. Either change would also add code to fix only the order of two error messages. No key is now accepted that was refused before. The builder's open issue, that the owner should confirm the C54 reading for the server config, still stands. The message is now clear, so what is left to confirm is only the order.
